topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory remarks and sets the context for studying the complement system.

topics.label: Fundamentals and core mechanics of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the general purpose, historical nomenclature, and central C3 activation mechanics of the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three upstream recognition pathways that drive the complement cascade to its activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream processes by which activated complement eliminates pathogens through opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation and protection against complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that prevent complement from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how genetic and acquired deficiencies in specific complement components result in distinct clinical phenotypes.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement attack
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the strategies and molecular mechanisms used by pathogens to resist and neutralize complement destruction.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session and previews the topic of the next lecture.
